name: Souls of Mischief
hook: Four East Oakland teenagers whose one perfect single, built on a jazz-fusion drummer's record, became the sound of 1993.

blurb.age7: Four friends from Oakland who were teenagers when they made a famous rap song called '93 'til Infinity'.
blurb.age13: A-Plus, Opio, Phesto and Tajai grew up in East Oakland and were part of Hieroglyphics, a group of rappers that also included Del the Funky Homosapien. In 1993, while still teenagers, they released '93 'til Infinity'. A-Plus built the beat from a 1974 record called 'Heather' by the drummer Billy Cobham, speeding up its slow bassline and marimba and adding his own drums. It's a relaxed, looping song about hanging out, and people still play it thirty years later.
blurb.adult: Souls of Mischief show the jazz-sample sound travelling west and staying distinct from the gangsta rap that dominated California rap commercially in 1993. The single's reputation has grown rather than faded: it placed fifth on Rolling Stone's 2023 list of the greatest West Coast hip-hop songs. Its beat is the first sample edge on this map where the source is a jazz-fusion record, which opens the sampled-artist hub pattern (Q21).
